title: ATP generation
cheat_card: ATP is generated via substrate-level phosphorylation (glycolysis & Krebs) and oxidative phosphorylation (chemiosmosis).
ETC complexes pump $H^+$ from the matrix into the intermembrane space, building an electrochemical proton gradient.
Protons diffuse down their gradient back into the matrix through the channel of ATP synthase, powering ATP synthesis.
Aerobic respiration has a 39% energy efficiency rate (harvesting 263 kcal of glucose's 686 kcal in 36 ATP), with the rest lost as heat.
memory_anchor:
Chemiosmosis:
Protons ($H^+$) pumped to Intermembrane Space -> Proton Motive Force -> Flow through ATP Synthase (like water through a turbine) -> Matrix -> ATP produced.

flashcards.q: How is the hydrogen ion ($H^+$) gradient established in the mitochondrion, and where is it most concentrated?
flashcards.a: The energy released from electrons flowing down the ETC is used by protein complexes to pump H+ from the matrix into the intermembrane space, where it becomes highly concentrated.

flashcards.q: Describe how ATP synthase utilizes the H+ gradient to generate ATP.
flashcards.a: ATP synthase contains a channel that allows H+ to flow down their electrochemical gradient back into the matrix. This flow of protons drives the enzyme to synthesize ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate (Pi).

flashcards.q: Calculate the approximate energy efficiency of aerobic cellular respiration if one mole of glucose contains 686 kcal and yields 36 ATP.
flashcards.a: Since each ATP phosphate bond stores 7.3 kcal, 36 ATP molecules yield 263 kcal. The efficiency is calculated as (263 / 686) * 100 = 39%, with the remaining 61% released as heat.

outline_blanks: During cellular respiration, the ETC pumps protons from the matrix into the [[intermembrane space]] to form a gradient. Protons then diffuse back through the [[ATP synthase]] channel to power phosphorylation. Aerobic respiration of one glucose molecule yields 36-38 ATP, representing an efficiency of [[39%]].
